title: Pill — The box measures. Pill explains.

slides.name: Title

els.text: CAL HACKS 13.0 · IDEA TO DEMO · FIGMA
A $40 lab-in-a-box. Drop one tablet in water, close the lid, and three minutes later it says PASS, NEEDS LAB or UNABLE TO VERIFY. In a clinic, that answer decides whether the supplier gets paid.

slides.notes: Open on the object. One tablet, about three minutes, one of three words. In clinic mode that word holds or releases a supplier's payment. Everything in this deck was generated from our repo by the Pill → Figma plugin.

slides.name: The problem

els.text: The instrument that catches a bad tablet in a lab costs $20,000 to $100,000 and sits far from the clinics that need it.
medical products in low- and middle-income countries estimated substandard or falsified
extra malaria deaths a year in sub-Saharan Africa, modelled, from substandard and falsified antimalarials (range 64,000–158,000)
children's deaths linked to contaminated cough syrups in three countries, 2022–23, most under five
spent each year on substandard and falsified medical products, by WHO's estimate

slides.notes: Numbers exactly as on our site, each with its source. 116,000 is the central estimate of a modelled range, 64,000 to 158,000. We do not animate these.

slides.name: The idea

els.text: Lot numbers can be copied. Dissolution cannot.
A recall lookup trusts the label. Pill measures the tablet itself: one tablet in 900 mL of water, a paddle at the same speed every run, two light sensors watching it dissolve.
A 465–475 nm LED shines across the cup. Riboflavin absorbs it as the tablet dissolves.
A second sensor behind green plastic sees the riboflavin glow. Chalk clouds the water; it does not glow.
Fig 1 · The station, drawn in code for the website: cup, blue LED, two sensors, thermistor, stepper paddle, ESP32, Pi touchscreen.

slides.notes: Why measurement beats lookup: the FDA found falsified product carrying a real lot number. Two channels: inline absorbance and 90° glow. The ESP32 measures; it decides nothing.

slides.name: How a run works

els.text: Ten reference runs make the band.
Photograph the bottle. Lot checked against the FDA recall list.
Dark, then blank. Lid open? The run does not start.
Drop one tablet. The paddle turns. The pill fills.
The curve flattens. Seven rules, in order. The rule that fired is printed.
The pill fill: how far this tablet has dissolved, as a % of the reference plateau.
Levels shown are an illustration; the app draws them live from the sensor stream.

slides.notes: The app shows the run as a pill filling to the reference plateau. At 100% the curve has flattened and the seven rules run. The verdict comes from deterministic rules, not from a model.

slides.name: Three answers

els.text: Plateau in the reference band and the glow rose with it (P1).
Light dropped with no glow, no plateau, or a plateau outside the band (N1–N3).
No reference for this drug, a fault, or too little data (U1–U3).
Seven rules, checked in order. A model writes the plain-English "why"; it never sets the verdict.

slides.notes: Three words only. PASS means this tablet's curve matched last night's riboflavin references on this box. It does not mean right drug, right dose or contaminant-free.

slides.name: Clinic mode

els.text: A clinic samples one tablet from each delivery. The policy agent reads the verdict, the recall check and the spend cap, and proposes release, hold or escalate. A pharmacist taps.
A release needs PASS, no recall record for the lot, amount within the spend cap, and the pharmacist’s tap.
NEEDS LAB: hold, and draft the lab referral with the curve attached.
UNABLE TO VERIFY: escalate to a person; no money moves.
A recall hit holds the payment regardless of the verdict.
Recall lookup unreachable: hold until a lookup succeeds or a human overrides.

slides.notes: policy.md, six clauses, quoted verbatim in the app. The model can only downgrade an outcome. Release always needs a person's tap. All money here is SANDBOX.

slides.name: Coinbase

els.text: Escrow → supplier in USDC on Base, only after PASS and a pharmacist’s tap.
No local reference? The agent pays another station’s /verify over x402, capped per day.
Every station can sell /verify: 402 → sign → settle → 200 with the verdict and the rule id.
site · what Coinbase is for here

slides.notes: Coinbase moves only the money the verdict decides. Testnet USDC on Base Sepolia; nothing here is real money. Spend caps live in a text file the judge can read.

slides.name: App screens

els.text: One app, the Pi touchscreen and the phone.
20 routes in React. All 173 app screenshots from our build passes (111 phone, 62 desktop) were imported into the Figma file automatically, one frame each, labelled with their route.

slides.notes: Same web app on the station's touchscreen and on any phone. The Design file has every screenshot on the "App screens" page, grouped by build pass, each frame linked to its route.

slides.name: Website

els.text: Built code-first (Vite + anime.js) after a 16-persona panel scored a plain, honest page 8.0 against a copied storytelling site at 3.7. First live at 00:52 Saturday.
Hero: the binary pill, drawn in characters. Words stay ink; colour lives in backgrounds and lines.

slides.notes: The website came first and set the tokens the app inherited.

slides.name: Workflow

els.text: Code first, then Figma from the code.
Figma styles + variables ↔ CSS via Composio
Pill → Figma plugin: design from code
Honest order: no Figma was used Friday or Saturday morning. The Figma files were generated from the repo afterwards, and the log says so.

slides.notes: We are a code-first team. Ideation and prototyping happened in markdown, AI panels and HTML. Figma enters as the place the repo is published to: slides, screens, tokens, ideation board.

slides.name: Design from code

els.text: Node, no npm deps; ffmpeg or sips for images
comment · dev resources · thumbnails · tokens → CSS

Recipe for code-first teams: keep the repo as the source of truth, emit one JSON, let a plugin draw it. One run gives designers editable layers, every screen, the tokens as styles, and a board of how you decided.
Why a plugin: the Figma REST API and our Composio connector can read, comment and set variables, but cannot create layers or slides. The Plugin API can.

slides.notes: The REST API cannot draw. So the repo emits deck.json and a 1-file plugin draws it in whichever editor it is opened in. Composio then closes the loop: comments, dev resources back to the code, thumbnails, and tokens back to CSS.

slides.name: Before and after

els.text: Per-unit figures are our assumption (20 min/slide, 1 min/screenshot, 1 min/token), not a measurement.
screenshots placed per run, no hand work (173 app, 106 site); 39 CSS variables become Figma styles + variables. Counted on the stub run.
Hand handoff drift: 8 of 27 site tokens reached the app unchanged, 7 changed value, 12 renamed or dropped.

slides.notes: Before numbers are estimates and say so. After numbers are measured on this machine; the real Figma run time is printed by the plugin.

slides.name: What PASS does not mean

els.text: Pill screens tablets. It does not certify them.
The dissolution curve of this one tablet, on this box, was consistent with last night's riboflavin reference runs. No red flags found.
That the tablet is the right drug, the right dose, or free of contaminants. Pill has one reference drug today. Anything it cannot compare goes to a lab, by design.
Results charts on our site are marked as an illustration until the calibration runs are on the page.

slides.notes: Say the limits before a judge asks. One reference drug (riboflavin). Charts marked illustration until real runs land.

slides.name: Ask and next

els.text: Ten riboflavin reference runs and chalk runs, plotted on the site in place of the illustration.
Each new drug needs its own band. Until then it is UNABLE TO VERIFY, on purpose.
A procurement officer samples one tablet per delivery; we log every decision and every override.
Ask: tell us which tablet to calibrate next, and introduce us to one clinic pharmacist.

slides.notes: Close on what is still not done and what we need.

rows.label: What we did
cells: Nine ideas were considered and six went through scored panels. FloodToll, DripGuard and Payout died on buildability or business. Lot beat Bill and Streets 13 votes of 16 and was renamed Pill. A second panel scored a plain, honest website 8.0 against a copied storytelling site at 3.7.

The prototype was the product. The phone mock on the site loops calibration, bottle, recall, run, verdict and release, and those loops became APP-PLAN's twelve screens. The binary-pill hero was tried as a standalone HTML file before it went on the site.

The site's 27 tokens seeded the app's 44. The plugin now puts the app's colour tokens into Figma as styles and variables, and the script reads them back as CSS, so a change made in Figma can land in code.

The app (20 routes), the x402/Nessie payment service and the Claude and Gemini wiring were generated against written plans. Then the repo generated its Figma: build-deck.mjs turns screenshots, CSS tokens, debate JSON and this log into deck.json; the plugin draws the Slides deck, the Design pages and the FigJam board.

rows.label: What broke
cells: Plain-page scores had a standard deviation of 0: sixteen voices, one opinion, and the docs say so. Two persona replies failed to parse. Nothing visual existed; the FigJam board was built afterwards from the JSON, not used live.

Nobody without a code editor could change the prototype or click through it, which is the gap the Figma Make prompt fills. The site went through four versions in 53 minutes; v3 dropped a section and recoloured, v4 moved colour off the words.

By hand, 8 of 27 tokens arrived identical, 7 changed value (some on purpose: the verdict colours were re-pointed at mint, amber and grey) and 12 were renamed or not needed (blue → sky, paper → bg). Nothing recorded which changes were intended. Composio's Figma tools read, comment and set variables but cannot draw a layer.

The scaffold's P6 rule held money only when the recall lookup was unreachable, so a delivery with no bottle attached could be proposed for release; a builder's end-to-end test caught it. A tail -6 cut off Vercel's output, the deploy was re-run, and we got two identical production deploys. The REST API cannot create nodes, hence a plugin.
